Smith.text: Many immigrants became Smiths: German Schmidt and its Polish equivalent Kowalski were often anglicized to it.
Smith.evidence: many immigrants did choose to begin their American lives with more "American" names, particularly with Anglicised versions of their birth names; the German Schmidt was often Anglicized to Smith not only during the world wars, but also commonly in times of peace, and the Polish equivalent Kowalski was Anglicized to Smith as well.

Johnson.text: It's also the usual American spelling of Johansson, the most common surname in Sweden.
Johnson.evidence: Johansson is a patronymic family name of Swedish origin meaning "son of Johan", or "Johan's son". It is the most common Swedish family name, followed by Andersson. ... while the most common spelling in the US is Johnson.

Williams.text: In the 2020 census it was the most common surname among Black Americans.
Williams.evidence: The table below presents the most common 100 surnames as of the 2020 Census. ... The most common name among black Americans was Williams and the most common name among Asian Americans was Nguyen.

Brown.text: It began as a nickname for brown hair, skin or clothes, and is now the most common surname in Jamaica.
Brown.evidence: Brown is an English-language surname in origin chiefly descriptive of a person with brown hair, complexion or clothing. ... It is the most common surname in Jamaica

Jones.text: It's not unusual for five or more of the Wales rugby team's starting XV to be called Jones.
Jones.evidence: It is not uncommon for five or more of the starting XV for the Wales national rugby union team to be named Jones.

Garcia.text: It may come from Basque words for "young" or "bear", and Edith Piaf's real surname, Gassion, is a cognate.
Garcia.evidence: Alfonso Irigoyen believed it to derive from the Basque adjective garze(a) meaning "young" ... Ramón Menéndez Pidal and Antonio Tovar suggested it may come from the Basque word (H)artz, meaning "(the) Bear". ... There are Gasconic cognates of Garcia like Gassie and Gassion (Béarn, Gassio 14th century, real name of Edith Piaf, born Edith Gassion).

Miller.text: It's the most common surname among the Amish, coming from Müller in Switzerland.
Miller.evidence: Miller is also the most common surname in the Amish, originating from Müller in Switzerland.

Rodriguez.text: In Belgium, the House of Rodriguez d'Evora y Vega were for generations the Great Breadmasters of Flanders.
Rodriguez.evidence: In Belgium the House of Rodriguez d'Evora y Vega was for generations Great Breadmaster of Flanders

Davis.text: Like its Welsh twin Davies, it may come from Dyfed, a medieval Welsh kingdom, or simply mean "son of David".
Davis.evidence: Davies is a patronymic Welsh surname meaning "son of David". ... In the United States, the variant "Davis" is much more common. ... The first theory states that it may stem from the Kingdom of Dyfed, a medieval Welsh kingdom located in modern-day Carmarthenshire

Martinez.text: It means "son of Martín", a name that goes back to Mars, the Roman god of war.
Martinez.evidence: It originated as a patronymic surname, meaning "son of Martín" ... Martínez comes from the personal name "Martin", itself derived from the Latin Martinus, whose root is Mars, the name of the Roman god of fertility and war.
